text:
ryan: Quick question for the SDK folks — should we converge on a small "Session" abstraction that owns transport handshake + fallback policy across Python/TS/Go? Thinking long-term this would simplify retries/pagination interactions.

mika: +1 on a tiny Session. main goals: 1) express fallback chain (hosted -> dedicated -> private) 2) attach per-request idempotency markers 3) surface simple backoff hooks.

anne: Curious how this interacts with pagination. If Session retries transparently, we need to guarantee page ordering and cursor stability. We can't accidentally return duplicate pages. :thinking_face:

ryan: Right — Session should expose two primitives: "transport.callUnary(req)" (idempotency-aware) and "transport.streamPages(req)" (cursor-aware, explicit resume token). retries for streamPages should be conservative: only retry before client-ack of page, otherwise surface an error and let client resume with server cursor.

sam: For language ergonomics: Python/TS can implement Session as a small object with async methods. Go needs to avoid allocation churn — make the retry policy pluggable but value-type friendly.

mika: Proposed minimal RetryPolicy shape (pseudocode):
```json
{
  "max_attempts": 5,
  "initial_backoff_ms": 100,
  "max_backoff_ms": 2000,
  "retryable_errors": ["UNAVAILABLE", "DEADLINE_EXCEEDED"]
}
```
We should also allow a per-call override.

anne: Important: distinguish transport-level idempotency vs application intents. Suggest we auto-add a monotonic request nonce for idempotent calls, but let users opt-out for non-idempotent ops.

ryan: Agree. Also need header propagation for routing hints (x-redwood-region, x-customer-tier). Session ought to take default headers and allow per-call augmentation.

sam: One tricky thing: hosted->dedicated fallback requires credentials/tenant scoping differences. Session needs to expose a light adapter that maps auth tokens + headers between tiers. That mapping should be explicit so languages can avoid hidden env fetches.

mika: On pagination semantics, my suggestion: streamPages yields a small envelope {page, resume_token_optional}. If transport retries before delivering page, Session can replay transparently. If failure after page delivered, client must call resume with token. This keeps semantics clear and avoids de-duplication complexity.

anne: For a migration path: start with TS and Python Session shims that wrap current clients. Keep the core retry engine in a shared design doc, then implement idiomatic bindings. Go can implement the same API but as interfaces + small helpers.

sam: Observability: Session should emit lightweight events: transport.start, transport.backoff, transport.fallback(which_tier), transport.success/failure. That will let Console show per-route fallback rates.

ryan: Perf note — don't put KV cache inside Session if it means cross-req locking. Instead, let Session expose cache hooks (get_prefix_cache, set_prefix_cache) so embedder can implement lock-free caches per language.

mika: Security: when falling to private deployments, we must clear any sensitive routing headers and use the tenant mapping adapter. Add a hard-coded hygiene check in Session that blocks header leakage unless explicit "allow_header_forwarding" is true.

anne: Edge case: pagination + function calling (chat+tools) where function results affect next page token. We'll need a test harness that simulates partial streams and server-driven cursors. Add to SDK e2e tests.

sam: Implementation checklist (short):
- design doc for Session API (shared)
- TS/Python prototypes (shims)
- Go idiomatic adapter (interface + small impl)
- tests: pagination-resume, hosted->dedicated fallback, header hygiene, metrics hooks

ryan: I'll draft the design doc tonight. rough outline: goals, primitives (callUnary, streamPages), RetryPolicy shape, header adapter, events, cache hooks, migration plan. Ping @anne @mika for review tomorrow.

deploy-bot: ryan pushed branch r/session-unify-392 -> staging (CI started).

mika: Nice. When you have the draft, add a tiny example for each language showing how a client would do a paginated call and a failover. That helps product folks understand the UX.

anne: Also include a short note about backwards compatibility: existing clients keep working; new Session is additive and can be opt-in via factory method.

ryan: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
